channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Past White House adviser Raj Panjabi has written a playbook for 'living room' crises
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi is the author of Safer: A Playbook. His goal is to help people face a personal crisis — health, workplace, family conflicts — and "turn fear into action."

item.title: Europe's crisis of discontent: Student and cost-of-living protests spread across EU
item.description: A growing wave of discontent is sweeping across Europe. What began in France as student protests over deteriorating school conditions, teacher shortages and an education system under pressure has quickly grown into something much bigger: a groundswell of discontent over the rising cost of living, unaffordable housing and struggling public services.

item.title: French 2027 presidential elections: Why Melenchon is a Gen Z favourite
item.description: Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon is beloved by French youth, but also one of the country’s most controversial politicians. His encouragement of the youth protests sweeping through France months ahead of the presidential election has only made him more divisive. So, why is Melenchon a Gen Z favourite? FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young supporters to find out.

item.title: WATCH: Multiple water rescues amid flood emergencies in the South
item.description: A flood emergency is underway across multiple states in the South – triggering dozens of water rescues in Florida, Georgia and Tennessee in the middle of the night.

item.title: Two men charged with murder after death of non-league footballer
item.description: Two men have been charged with murder after the death of a non-league footballer.

item.title: Premier League footballer sparks police operation after bow and arrow sighting
item.description: Newcastle United's Bosnian full-back Amar Dedic reportedly found himself at the centre of a major police response after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows in the countryside.

item.title: Childminder who neglected more than 20 children jailed
item.description: A childminder who admitted wilfully neglecting and abandoning children in her care has been jailed for two years.

item.title: WATCH: These identical twin sisters speak at the same time
item.description: Danny New talks to identical twin sisters in Australia who are turning heads for their unique speech patterns.

item.title: Bus whose passengers included kids crashes in France, leaving 2 dead and 16 injured
item.description: A bus crash in eastern France has killed one minor and one young adult

item.title: Judge blocks Trump arch hours after federal panel approval
item.description: Ahead of the vote to grant final approval, the Vietnam vet leading a lawsuit to stop the project called it "frankly blasphemous."

item.title: Poundland owner seeks private MP session 'to avoid show trial'
item.description: Poundland's owner is seeking to give evidence to MPs in private next week as it seeks to avoid an evidence session on the discount retailer's fate turning into "a show trial".

item.title: Midterms over, Democrats eye wide-open 2028 White House race
item.description: With the US midterms over, Democrats are turning to what could become one of their most crowded and unpredictable presidential primaries in decades, a 2028 contest ​likely to expose the party's divide over how to win back the White House. Despite their resounding victories on Tuesday, Democrats enter the 2028 campaign still divided over whether to tack to the center or move further left on issues ranging from healthcare and taxes to policing and foreign policy.

item.title: Israel president to announce Sunday who will form new government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday, November 8, whom he will task with trying to form a new government, following post-election talks with all party leaders. 46 parliament members recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, while 67 backed his opponent Gadi Eisenkot. Seven lawmakers abstained.

item.title: US Republicans face reckoning after major midterm election defeat
item.description: Following the Democrats' sweeping victory in Tuesday's US midterm elections, Republicans are facing a moment of reckoning. With Donald Trump now a "lame-duck" president, the party must find a way forward after a historic electoral setback. The GOP faces major questions about how to win back voters and who will lead the party, with the next presidential election just two years away.

item.title: At least two killed, 16 injured in school bus accident in eastern France
item.description: A bus carrying school children crashed south of Bourg-en-Bresse in eastern France on Friday, killing at least two people and injuring 16 others. The vehicle was carrying 43 passengers in total.

item.title: Pollution, shortages, crime: Daily life in Pakistan's megacity Karachi
item.description: Fed up with hours of power cuts, the residents of Pakistan's economic hub Karachi took to the streets in recent days and blocked several major roads. The outburst of anger highlights the daily problems faced by a megacity of over 21 million people, which has once again been ranked among the world's least liveable cities.

item.title: Death toll rises to 50 in Russian attack on aid distribution ‌point in Ukraine
item.description: The death toll from Russia's bombing of an aid ​distribution ‌point in ⁠Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday ‌has risen to 50, Kyiv's Emergency Service said on Friday, making it ​one of the deadliest strikes ‌on civilians this year.

item.title: Uncertainty over Nigeria vote as court bars opposition leader
item.description: A Nigerian court Thursday declared invalid the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as the presidential candidate for the opposition African Democratic Congress, just two months before the country's elections. The party, which accused the ruling All Progressives Congress of involvement in the lawsuit, will appeal, its spokesman said – but the ruling creates legal headaches for Abubakar and uncertainty for voters with the January 16 vote around the corner.

item.title: Ethiopia clashes drive thousands into Kenya
item.description: Deadly clashes between armed forces in southern Ethiopia have driven tens of thousands into neighbouring Kenya with no idea when they can safely return home. Ethiopia, Africa's second most populous country with around 130 million people, is grappling with multiple armed conflicts, particularly along borders between its states.

item.title: Navi Pillay on the ICC and accusations of bias against Africa
item.description: Former ICC judge and UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Navi Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her work promoting peace and international law. The South African jurist has spent decades fighting impunity, from apartheid-era abuses to the Rwandan genocide. But the International Criminal Court has faced persistent criticism in Africa, particularly over the perception that it has disproportionately targeted African leaders. FRANCE 24’s Clarisse Fortune spoke to Navi Pillay and asked her whether that criticism is justified.

item.title: Making history in Dakar 2026: Six young refugees, one Olympic dream
item.description: The medals are already being won at Dakar 2026. But beyond the scores and the celebrations, some athletes have overcome far greater challenges. Members of the first Refugee Youth Olympic Team, now living in Uganda and Kenya’s Kakuma Refugee Camp after fleeing conflict, are proving that the Games are about much more than sport.

item.title: Mass protests sweep France as huge crowds demand higher wages
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of striking workers protested across France on Thursday, November 5, against the rising cost of living following weeks of youth-led demonstrations, with police firing tear gas as clashes broke out in some cities. FRANCE 24's Emily Boyle reports.

item.title: California governor says commuting all death sentences in state
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom said Thursday, November 5, he was commuting all death sentences across the state to life imprisonment, in a move that will affect over 500 prisoners. FRANCE 24's correspondent Wassim Cornet reports.

item.title: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot secures broad backing in bid to form government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday, November 8, whom he will task with trying to form a new government, after the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot secured a commanding number of recommendations to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.title: 'Ramayana': Ancient Hindu epic and India's most expensive film
item.description: A big-budget film adaptation of the Ramayana, one of Hinduism's most revered epics, has renewed attention on the ancient tale that continues to shape India's culture, identity and politics. "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend", featuring Bollywood star Ranbir Kapoor, was released in India on Thursday, November 5, two days before the country's biggest festival of Diwali.

item.title: Low birth rates were emptying public schools. ICE deportations are now making it worse
item.description: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse.

item.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: Vance says they lost the midterms because of ____
item.description: Plus: Heidi Klum's hand, hackers and the pope's visitor!

item.title: 'Sleazy', 'manipulative' and 'ruthless': Russell Brand convicted of rape, sexual assault
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 6: Italian, British, French and Bulgarian papers discuss the bomb threats that diverted multiple flights across Europe on Thursday. British papers discuss Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault conviction. Finally, kids in Hanoi chase tourists – not for money, but for vocabulary. Bonus: we learn a fun fact about chihuahuas.

item.title: Two 16 year olds charged after five boys seriously injured at Halloween party
item.description: Two 16 year olds have been charged after five boys were seriously injured at a party on Halloween.

item.description: Raman is poised to become the 44th mayor of the nation’s second-largest city.

item.title: Live: European stocks plunge after US midterm election results shock markets
item.description: European shares tumbled on Friday as global investors grappled with uncertainty over AI stocks, following the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the US midterm elections. The drop is partly due to fears that Democrats could curb the development of AI data centres, which are widely unpopular among US voters. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: After cancer surgery, Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America with a visit to Uruguay, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question.

item.title: Trump calls midterms 'crooked', demands Alaska votes go to Republican candidate
item.description: Despite having previously accepted the US midterm election results, President Donald Trump told reporters on Thursday the elections were "crooked", and he demanded the remaining votes for Alaska go to its incumbent Republican senator.

item.title: Left-leaning Washington, Colorado join conservative states in banning trans athletes
item.description: Voters in Washington and Colorado have approved measures to ban transgender athletes from participating in school sports

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo brings his international football career to an end
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday, ending his 23-year career with Portugal. At 41, the Al-Nassr forward leaves the national team with 234 caps and 146 goals, both world records. As captain, he helped Portugal win Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025. The decision comes after several weeks of tensions with head coach Jorge Jesus, following Ronaldo's departure from the Portugal squad in September.

item.title: South Africa's ANC party on track to face 'nightmare' losses in municipal elections
item.description: South Africa's African National Congress party could face its worst-ever election result on Friday, with early counting suggesting it received only 32% ‌of the vote in the country’s municipal elections. Over two-thirds of votes have been counted so far, and the final results are expected later in the day.

item.title: 'Leaders all over the world understand that Trump is only there for two more years & then he's gone'
item.description: In American politics, even presidential power has its limits. And now, the laws of political gravity may finally be catching up with Donald Trump's hyper-aggressive exercise of executive authority. Following what political scientist Ian Bremmer describes as the most consequential electoral reversal for a governing party in more than half a century, the president and founder of Eurasia Group and GZERO Media argues that the United States has entered a new political phase: the beginning of the end of Trump's ability to dominate the political agenda, at home and on the world stage.

item.title: Andrew made more than £2,000 a month subletting Royal Lodge cottages
item.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor received more than £2,000 a month from renting out three cottages at his former Royal Lodge home, a report by the public spending watchdog has revealed.

item.description: The suspect was also killed in the gunfire, a police official said.

item.description: The Trump administration hoped to begin construction immediately after a federal panel approved its arch late Thursday. But just after midnight, the judge issued an order blocking work for 14 days.

item.description: Asian tech stocks fell sharply on Friday, driven by fears of tighter AI regulation following Democrats’ US midterm election victory. US voters widely oppose Data centres, and many winning candidates pledged to curb their development.
